summary.value: The New Hampshire, often called the New Hampshire Red, is an American chicken bred from Rhode Island Reds in the early 1900s. Farmers and researchers in New Hampshire picked birds that grew, feathered and matured faster, and the APA accepted the breed in 1935. It is lighter red than its parent stock, with black in the tail and wings, and the sun can fade it further. Roosters weigh about 8.5 pounds and hens about 6.5. Hens lay around 200 to 220 large brown eggs a year, and many go broody and raise chicks well. The breed serves for both meat and eggs and suits pasture flocks. Temperament depends on the line: some birds are gentle, others pushy toward calmer breeds. It handles cold winters well and copes with warm areas given good housing. It is the official state poultry of New Hampshire.
